issue.title: Full just test run fails ~60 gate/ops/launch tests via live host runtime-path contamination, unrelated to diff under test
issue.description:
DISCOVERED while running the full `just test` suite (not the required `just check` scoped lane) as extra diligence while implementing the approved plan sase/repos/plans/202608/adaptive_models_panel_description_height.md (Launch Control description-height change touching only src/sase/ace/tui/modals/models_panel_display.py, src/sase/ace/tui/styles.tcss, and Models-panel tests). `just test-scoped` (the actual required `just check` test lane) passed 745/745 clean; `just test-visual` passed 684/684 clean. The full `just test` run failed 60 tests, 30545 passed, 10 skipped, all in files unrelated to the diff: tests/test_gate_cli_answer.py, tests/test_gate_cli_act.py, tests/gate_conformance/test_gate_conformance.py (every cli-* and ace-* case), tests/main/test_ops_commands.py, tests/test_special_cases.py, tests/test_partial_launch_cleanup.py, tests/test_prompt_inputs.py, tests/test_multi_prompt_e2e.py, tests/ace/tui/modals/test_snippet_name_modal.py.

ROOT CAUSE (partially diagnosed, reproduced in isolation): re-running two of the failing tests together in isolation (tests/test_gate_cli_answer.py::test_set_types_every_declared_input_field + tests/test_special_cases.py::test_launch_query_from_agent_context_requests_approval) reproduces both failures deterministically. test_special_cases reveals real contamination: the mocked create_launch_approval_request_from_prompt is called with THIS actual live agent session's real prompt text ('#gh:sase The last model in the model pool shown in #sshot is cut off...') instead of the test's own literal input string, proving some code path under test reads real, live host session state (this very running sase agent's own launch/session data) rather than being fully isolated from environment. test_gate_cli_answer fails with `sase.ops.errors.OperationIOError: operation sidecar /home/bryan/.sase/procs/runtime/<real-pid>/operation-request.json has operation 'run.launch', expected 'gate.answer'` -- a real path under the live ~/.sase/procs/runtime tree, not a tmp_path fixture. A second isolated repro (tests/main/test_ops_commands.py::test_patch_status_success_and_failure_results) shows the SAME operation-mismatch error even though that test's result path is a fresh pytest tmp_path (`/tmp/pytest-of-bryan/.../ok.json`) with content `operation: 'run.launch'` -- meaning code under test wrote (or resolved) the wrong sidecar despite an explicit path argument, strongly suggesting a global/env-var-driven operation-context resolution (e.g. a real SASE_PROC_ID/operation-sidecar env var set in this live host shell) that these tests do not fully override via monkeypatch, so under `just test`'s parallel/full-process conditions the tests intermittently observe or write against this live host's actual 'run.launch' operation state instead of their own mocked/fixture state.

This differs from the already-tracked sase-lc (dirty-workspace source-tree audits contaminating the flake-baseline store) -- that bug is about audit tests reading an agent's own uncommitted source edits; this bug is about operation/gate/launch-CLI tests reading real live ~/.sase/procs/runtime state from the actual host session rather than being hermetically isolated, which only manifests when running the full unscoped suite (never observed in `just test-scoped` or `just test-visual`). Searched for existing task beads with 'gate_cli_answer', 'gate_conformance', 'test_ops_commands', 'operation sidecar', 'OperationIOError', 'run.launch' -- none found; also swept task beads created in the last 3 days and found only the related-but-distinct sase-lc.

IMPACT: blocks `just check-full` / plain `just test` from completing cleanly for any agent working from a live, actively-running host session (as opposed to a disposable CI sandbox), even on an otherwise clean diff. Project guidance already routes check-full through `/sase_monitor`, which may avoid this by running out-of-process, but the underlying hermeticity gap in these ops/gate/launch tests should be fixed directly.

REPRODUCTION: from a live sase agent shell, run e.g. `.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/test_gate_cli_answer.py::test_set_types_every_declared_input_field tests/main/test_ops_commands.py::test_patch_status_success_and_failure_results -q` and observe the OperationIOError 'run.launch' mismatch; or the full `just test` lane.

payload.entry: RELATED: sase-lc — different mechanism (dirty-tree audit contamination of flake-baseline store vs. live ~/.sase/procs/runtime state bleeding into gate/ops/launch CLI tests), but both are examples of a live/dirty agent workspace polluting full-suite test results; a shared fix theme (stronger test isolation from the live host session) may be worth considering together.

evidence.note: Independent reproduction on HEAD c6d84d2a4: just test-scoped escalated to the full lane because core identity changed and produced the same host-runtime contamination signature — 59 failures across partial launch cleanup, special cases, ops commands, gate CLI act/answer, gate conformance, multi-prompt launch, and prompt inputs. Failure payloads read this live agent's real LaunchApproval prompt and run.launch operation state. The run still passed 30,618 tests; my diff touches only the two Models-panel display modules, and all 313 focused Models-panel tests pass.

Proposed by sase-mf.4 and independently reproduced by sase-mf.land on current master 3c3909c31 after just install: .venv/bin/pytest -q tests/test_gate_cli_answer.py tests/test_config.py yields 17 gate-answer failures / 34 passes; every failure reads the live /home/bryan/.sase/procs/runtime/vna5a0werb03/operation-request.json with operation run.launch instead of the fixture's gate.answer sidecar. This exactly matches sase-ml's host-runtime contamination root cause.

Independently reproduced on master d22622365 while landing epic sase-m6.6.1. A full 'just test' run failed 83 tests / 45 errors; re-running the failing files with only the six SASE_PROC_* env vars unset (env -u SASE_PROC_REQUEST_PATH -u SASE_PROC_RESULT_PATH -u SASE_PROC_ID -u SASE_PROC_OPERATION -u SASE_PROC_LOG_PATH -u SASE_PROC_SESSION_ID) turned 55 of those failures green in one pass: tests/gate_conformance (28), tests/test_gate_cli_answer.py (17), tests/test_gate_cli_act.py (4), tests/main/test_ops_commands.py (6) all passed 77/77+3 skipped, and tests/test_special_cases.py, tests/test_prompt_inputs.py, tests/test_partial_launch_cleanup.py, tests/test_multi_prompt_e2e.py, tests/test_config_cache.py passed too. This pins the contamination to environment inheritance rather than xdist contention: src/sase/ops/cli.py:resolve_request_path falls back to os.environ[SASE_PROC_REQUEST_PATH], so any pytest process launched inside a live SASE agent proc resolves that agent's own /home/bryan/.sase/procs/runtime/<id>/operation-request.json and fails with OperationIOError: has operation 'run.launch', expected 'gate.answer'. A conftest-level scrub of SASE_PROC_* (and any other operation-context env) would fix all 55 at once. Reported by the sase-m6.6.1 land agent.

payload.entry: Supplementary evidence from epic sase-mf's land pass on rebased master 0f63a62ab (workspace sase_17): 'just test-scoped' escalated to the full 30,699-test lane; 33 failures fall in this bead's cluster (test_gate_conformance 28, test_gate_cli_answer 17 -- wait, exact split: gate_conformance 28, gate_cli_answer 17, ops_commands 6, gate_cli_act 4, plus one each in test_special_cases, test_prompt_inputs, test_partial_launch_cleanup, test_multi_prompt_e2e, test_config, test_config_cache, modals/test_snippet_name_modal). Attribution is clean because the tree under test changed only 2 memory .md files and 152 PNG goldens -- no Python, YAML, or config source. The remaining 52 non-visual failures/errors in that same run are a separate PatchFilterBar shared-page teardown cluster recorded on active plan sase-m6.6.1.

evidence.note:
Independent reproduction at master d22622365 (workspace sase_12, 2026-08-16), while splitting src/sase/bead/_stream_integrity.py (bead-store code only; no gate/ops/launch files touched). 'just check' escalated to the full lane: 83 failed, 30767 passed, 10 skipped, 45 errors in 349s; all 13 lint gates green. The gate/ops/launch subset matches this bead's named files exactly: tests/test_gate_cli_answer.py (17 nodes), tests/test_gate_cli_act.py (4), tests/gate_conformance/test_gate_conformance.py, tests/main/test_ops_commands.py (6), tests/test_special_cases.py::test_launch_query_from_agent_context_requests_approval, tests/test_partial_launch_cleanup.py::test_launch_query_prints_each_launched_agent_pid, tests/test_prompt_inputs.py, tests/test_multi_prompt_e2e.py.

NEW EVIDENCE — not parallel-lane-dependent: with my changes stashed (pristine master), '.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/test_config_cache.py tests/main/test_ops_commands.py tests/ace/tui/test_jump_to_changespec.py -q -p no:randomly' (45 tests, serial, no xdist) still failed 7, including all 6 test_ops_commands nodes. So the contamination reproduces in a small SERIAL run, which rules out xdist ordering/parallelism as a necessary condition and strengthens the live-host-state theory in this bead's description: the failing assertions again showed this live agent session's real prompt text (the '#gh:sase Something is wrong with the bead store...' epic-launch prompt for sase-mn) substituted for the test's own literal input.

Independent reproduction on current workspace while splitting cli_work_cleanup.py: required 'just check' escalated to 1,417 tests and failed only tests/test_special_cases.py::test_launch_query_from_agent_context_requests_approval. The mocked approval creator received this live agent's real operation prompt instead of the test literal. The node failed again alone with SASE_PROC_REQUEST_PATH inherited, then passed 1/1 with only that variable unset. The refactor touches bead-work cleanup modules, not query launch or ops request loading.

Independent corroboration from epic sase-mq's landing agent: two phases of epic sase-mq (Enforce user-owned primary workspace boundaries) hit this same contamination in separate workspaces and separately filed it as PROPOSED FOLLOW-UP. sase-mq.1 (2026-08-16T04:43:26Z) recorded that its escalated suite left 60 failures, all gate/ops/launch tests reading /home/bryan/.sase/procs/runtime/vna5a0werb03/operation-request.json — this agent's own live run.launch sidecar — polluting gate.act/gate.answer and ops commands. sase-mq.4 (2026-08-16T07:44:30Z) independently reproduced the same class (gate CLI, gate conformance, and tests/main/test_ops_commands.py) and explicitly noted it reproduces on clean master, unrelated to the approval-launches diff under test. Impact confirmed on this landing: the failure set is large enough (60-93 failures across four separate check-full runs during this epic) that every phase agent had to hand-triage it before landing, and it masks real regressions in the same run.

Independent reproduction from land agent sase-mq.8.land on master d10fe53024144a0084501c349642552cccc8e033 after successful just install: .venv/bin/python -m pytest -q tests/test_gate_cli_answer.py::test_set_types_every_declared_input_field fails by reading the live /home/bryan/.sase/procs/runtime/vna5a0werb03/operation-request.json with operation 'run.launch' instead of 'gate.answer'; rerunning the exact node with SASE_PROC_REQUEST_PATH, SASE_PROC_RESULT_PATH, SASE_PROC_ID, SASE_PROC_OPERATION, SASE_PROC_LOG_PATH, and SASE_PROC_SESSION_ID unset passes 1/1. This disposes the same PROPOSED FOLLOW-UP reported independently by child phases sase-mq.8.1, sase-mq.8.3, and sase-mq.8.4.

payload.entry: Supplementary landing evidence after post-close cleanup for sase-mq.8: required just check escalated because Justfile changed and reproduced this exact host runtime-path contamination cluster (60 failed, 30,896 passed, 10 skipped), including gate CLI/conformance, ops commands, launch, prompt, and config tests reading run.launch operation state. All 147 tests in every failed file family then passed both serially and with -n 14 once the six SASE_PROC_* variables were explicitly unset; the directly modified lease/ownership modules passed 33/33 and Symvision passed. This agent already supplied +1 evidence at 2026-08-16T10:16Z, so this is a supplementary note rather than a duplicate +1 or new task. The causal active epic sase-m9.3.1 already carries this landing's DISCOVERED ISSUE note.

evidence.note: Independent reproduction during ctrl_space_stale_prompt_context implementation on 2026-08-16: required just check passed all lint gates, escalated to the governed full test lane because of core-identity-changed selection, then failed 59 gate/ops/launch tests (tests/gate_conformance, tests/test_gate_cli_answer.py, tests/test_gate_cli_act.py, tests/main/test_ops_commands.py, tests/test_special_cases.py, tests/test_prompt_inputs.py, tests/test_partial_launch_cleanup.py, tests/test_multi_prompt_e2e.py) with the same inherited SASE_PROC_* operation-sidecar contamination pattern. The focused regression suite for this change passed 102 tests before the full-lane failure, and this diff does not touch gate/ops CLI sidecar resolution.

INDEPENDENT EVIDENCE (write direction, durable proof): while root-causing a phantom 'running proc' in ACE on 2026-08-16, found that pytest processes do not merely READ live ~/.sase/procs state — they WRITE rows into the user's real proc store, and those rows persist. /home/bryan/.sase/procs/procs.jsonl contained 21 kind='tui', lifecycle='legacy' rows whose cwd is an ephemeral agent workspace (sase_14, sase_15, sase_16, sase_17, sase_19, sase_20) rather than a real checkout, carrying unmistakable test-fixture payloads: label 'kill my_feature' (the my_feature fixture agent used by tests/test_agent_kill_single_actions.py) and message 'Kill cleanup failed for my_feature: boom' (a test double raising Exception('boom')). One of those leaked rows (proc_id hbw7szt6mnbh, session 20260816T013806Z-2654527, pid 2654527, started 2026-08-16T01:39:49Z) was still status='running' with finished_at=null roughly twelve hours later, its pid long dead. It inflated the live ACE session's top-bar proc indicator to 1 while the Admin Center Procs tab (session-scoped) correctly showed 0 running, and it blocked a completed 'sase update' from restarting ACE, because the restart gate treats any projected running row as a blocker.

MECHANISM: unlike the bead store (assert_bead_store_write_sandboxed) and telemetry (assert_test_state_write_isolated), the proc store has NO write guard. src/sase/procs/store.py resolves proc_store_path() and calls straight into the Rust binding from append_proc/reserve_proc/update_proc/finish_proc with no pytest-sandbox check. tests/_conftest_environment.py isolates SASE_HOME per test via monkeypatch, so any write that lands AFTER fixture teardown — a thread worker or Textual worker still running, e.g. the submit worker _submit_durable_proc spawns at src/sase/ace/tui/actions/proc_actions.py:273 — resolves the REAL ~/.sase and writes there. That teardown-race path exists at HEAD, so this is not confined to the older ACE mirror writer that produced these particular rows.

SUGGESTED REMEDIATION (same boundary this bead needs): give proc state under ~/.sase/procs the fail-closed guard the bead/telemetry stores already have, so a pytest process either writes inside SASE_PYTEST_SANDBOX_DIR or raises. That would have turned this silent corruption of the user's real store into a loud test failure, and it covers both the read contamination this bead reports and the write leak reported here.

IMPACT: silent corruption of the user's production proc store by test runs, plus a user-visible ACE defect (phantom running-proc count, blocked post-update restart). No new task bead created; a separate tale plan covers the ACE-side reconciliation and count-consistency fixes for the symptom.

Independent reproduction while implementing plan_archive_publication_recovery on 2026-08-16: required just check escalated to the full 8073-test lane (broadening-set / stale baseline) and failed 57 tests. Cluster matches this bead exactly: tests/gate_conformance, tests/test_gate_cli_answer.py, tests/test_gate_cli_act.py, tests/main/test_ops_commands.py, and tests/test_special_cases.py::test_launch_query_from_agent_context_requests_approval. Failures read this live agent's /home/bryan/.sase/procs/runtime/2ae7btcgz5te/operation-request.json (operation 'run.launch') or injected this session's real plan-archive diagnosis prompt into the launch-approval mock. One additional failure (tests/test_tui_plan_approval_archive.py) was a real regression in this diff and is fixed separately. This change does not touch ops/gate sidecar resolution.

CONFIRMED ROOT CAUSE with a controlled A/B — the leaked variables are SASE_PROC_REQUEST_PATH / SASE_PROC_RESULT_PATH / SASE_PROC_ID (src/sase/ops/models.py:12-15). Independent repro: 'just check-full' via /sase_monitor from a live agent (monitor 563h2j93e61t, 2026-08-16T14:05Z, workspace sase_15 on 78a9130f7) failed 72/30915. My agent shell had SASE_PROC_REQUEST_PATH=/home/bryan/.sase/procs/runtime/kq6tayvcwdkh/operation-request.json with SASE_PROC_OPERATION=run.launch — byte-for-byte the path in every 'OperationIOError: ... has operation run.launch, expected gate.answer' failure. sase/ops/cli.py:85 load_request() -> resolve_request_path() falls back to os.environ.get(REQUEST_ENV) when no -Q/--request-path is given, so the monitor subprocess inherited MY live agent's sidecar. This CONFIRMS the bead's 'strongly suggesting a global/env-var-driven operation-context resolution' hypothesis and names the variables. PROOF (A/B, same tree, same commit): running the 13 failing files with the vars inherited reproduces the failures; 'env -u SASE_PROC_REQUEST_PATH -u SASE_PROC_RESULT_PATH -u SASE_PROC_ID -u SASE_PROC_OPERATION -u SASE_PROC_LOG_PATH -u SASE_PROC_SESSION_ID .venv/bin/python -m pytest <13 files> -n 8' gives 240 passed, 3 skipped, 1 failed — and that single remaining failure was a genuine unrelated stale assertion I fixed. So 71 of the 72 failures are 100 percent this bug. NOTE: /sase_monitor does NOT avoid this (the bead speculated it might) — the monitor supervisor inherits the launching agent's SASE_PROC_* rather than scoping its own. SUGGESTED FIX: an autouse conftest fixture that monkeypatch.delenv's every SASE_PROC_* var, so ambient operation context can never reach a test; a targeted workaround for agents needing a clean full suite today is the 'env -u ...' prefix above.
